doc.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe Interview, 1961-11-25
doc.interviewee: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe

title: Passing the kitty and the Jaffes' double lives
summary: No admission, only a kitty; they hold day jobs, work long hours unpaid, and feel privileged.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But there's something interesting that you do over here, it's sort of hard to describe. You, you don't charge anything to get in, but you sort of pass the kitty. Can, can you actually make enough on this to pay the musicians? What about it, Sandra? Sometimes. Um, Saturday nights we usually do. And on Friday nights, well, the past two weeks have been rather slow, but our first two months here we've been able to meet expenses. Um, we thought about charging an admission, but there are a lot of problems involved once we do that. And we're going to be waiting a while and see how the unorthodox procedure of our business goes. If it goes alright and if we're able to meet expenses, we're going to keep it at kitty contributions. Well now, both of you are holding down outside jobs, and this means that you work normal hours from 9 to 5, and then you come down here starting at 8.30 and run until 12.30, right?
Well doesn't this get a little complicated, Alan? How can you, how can you manage a, a life of your own? And, aside from this, the actual working hours, it's, it's the coordinating.
It's not really complicated at all, you just, you just forget about your private life.
You throw it out the window? Yes. Well do you feel as if you're, uh, sort of crusading?

It's a silly question. No, not really. What do people do? It's funny that, uh, I think both of us feel, you know, quite privileged that we're able to be able to do this. The musicians are fine people, they're people who it's really an honor to be associated with. And, to be able to do what we're doing, even though it's long hours and we're not paying ourselves any salaries, and not really making anything, in fact, at times costing us something, other than just our time, uh, it's still just a thrill to hear these men play, to, to hear a new musician, to hear people improve from playing frequently.
